name: Alaska

sales.rateNote: Alaska levies no statewide sales tax. Boroughs and cities may levy their own sales and use taxes, so the rate depends entirely on the delivery address (0% in areas without a local tax).

local.levies: borough sales and use taxes (AS 29.45.650) and city sales and use taxes (AS 29.45.700); remote sales are collected through the Alaska Remote Seller Sales Tax Commission for member jurisdictions
local.capNote: No statutory maximum rate; each borough or city sets its rate, exemptions and any per-sale tax cap by ordinance.

groceries.note: No state tax. Local sales taxes may apply to food depending on the borough or city ordinance; purchases paid with SNAP or WIC benefits cannot be taxed locally.

clothing.note: No state tax; local sales taxes may apply.

sales.holidayNote: No statewide sales tax, so no state sales tax holiday.

useTax.note: No state use tax. A borough or city levying a sales tax may levy a use tax at the same rate, with credit for sales tax paid elsewhere.

facts.text: Boroughs may tax sales, rents and services; cities may levy sales taxes inside or outside a borough (AS 29.45.650 and 29.45.700).
Purchases made with SNAP food stamps or WIC vouchers cannot be subject to borough or city sales tax.
Since February 2020, member jurisdictions of the Alaska Remote Seller Sales Tax Commission collect local sales tax on online purchases, sourced to the point of delivery.
Remote sellers must register with ARSSTC once they exceed $100,000 of annual sales into Alaska; the 200-transaction test was dropped on January 1, 2025.
Many Alaska ZIP codes are larger than taxing boundaries, so buyers outside a taxing area can be wrongly charged; ARSSTC's official tax map and refund form address this.
Interest on late municipal sales tax may not exceed 15% a year.

property.levied: Local: boroughs and cities levy property tax (many areas levy none). The state itself levies only an oil and gas production and pipeline property tax of 20 mills (AS 43.56).

assessment.text: Property is assessed at its full and true (market) value as of January 1 of the assessment year. A municipality may not levy more than 3% (30 mills) of assessed value in a year.

homestead.name: Senior citizen and disabled veteran exemption
homestead.text: The first $150,000 of assessed value of the primary residence of a resident aged 65 or older, a disabled veteran, or a surviving spouse aged 60+ is exempt by state law. There is no general statewide homestead exemption for other owners.
homestead.applyBy: Written application to the local assessor; each municipality sets procedures and deadlines by ordinance.

otherRelief.name: Optional residential exemption
otherRelief.text: With voter approval, a municipality may exempt up to $75,000 of assessed value per residence (indexable to the Urban Alaska CPI).

otherRelief.name: Senior vehicle exemption
otherRelief.text: One motor vehicle per household owned by a resident aged 65+ is exempt from property tax or from the vehicle registration tax.

facts.text: A municipality may not levy property tax above 3% of assessed value (30 mills) in a year.
Municipalities also face a per-capita cap: total tax revenue may not exceed $1,500 per resident a year.
The state levies 20 mills on oil and gas production and pipeline property; local tax paid on that property is credited against it.
Municipalities may require seniors to be eligible for the Permanent Fund Dividend to claim the $150,000 exemption.
Value is set as of January 1 at the price a willing buyer would pay a willing seller on the open market.

uncertain: The DCCED Office of the State Assessor site (commerce.alaska.gov, Alaska Taxable report) blocks automated access (HTTP 403, DataDome): number of municipalities levying sales or property tax and statewide totals not verified.
Prescription drug and grocery treatment is set by each local ordinance; 'exempt' here means no state tax only.
Property tax due dates are set by each municipality; no statewide date exists.
The ARSSTC (intergovernmental commission of Alaska municipalities) is used for remote-seller rules and the tax map; it is not a state agency.
